knowledge_point.title: Finding an Area by Transforming to a Type I Region

question.:question/problem:
Using the change of variables 

$$
u=3 x - 2 y,\,v=x + y,
$$

calculate the area of the finite region $D$ bounded by the curve $(3 x - 2 y)^{2}-(x + y)=0$ and the line $x + y=25.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The area of the required region is given by

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows: 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required area, we will use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$  

Note that the changes of variables

$$
u=3 x - 2 y,\,v=x + y
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required area, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Substituting $3 x - 2 y=u$ and $x + y=v$ into the equation of the first curve, we get

$$
(3 x - 2 y)^{2}-(x + y)=0\,⟹\,u^{2}-v=0\,⟹\,v=u^{2}.
$$

while substituting $x + y=v$ into the equation of the second curve, we obtain

$$
v=25.
$$

To find the intersections of the curves in the $uv$-plane, we solve the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\{\begin{aligned}v=u^{2} \\ v=25\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,u=\pm 5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection points are $(\pm 5,25).$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane has the type I representation

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,-5\le u\le 5,\,u^{2}\le v\le 25\}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/repairs/2026-10-20-early-cohort/jobs/17592186129197/review-1-policy-2-6d8162cdaa407593/runtime/plots/05e61fee7d7ca9a1770b6259.png)

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x}&\frac{∂u}{∂y}\\\frac{∂v}{∂x}&\frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{matrix}\right| \\ &=\left|\begin{matrix}3&-2\\1&1\end{matrix}\right| \\ &=5\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=(5)^{-1}=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$  In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Compute the required area.

We calculate the required area by performing the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_D dxdy &=\iint_Δ |\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,dudv \\ &=\iint_Δ |\frac{1}{5}|\,dudv \\ &=\frac{1}{5}\int_{-5}^{5}[\int_{u^{2}}^{25}dv]du \\ &=\frac{1}{5}\int_{-5}^{5}[v]_{u^{2}}^{25}du \\ &=\frac{1}{5}\int_{-5}^{5}(25)-(u^{2})du \\ &=\frac{1}{5}\int_{-5}^{5}(25 - u^{2})du \\ &=\frac{1}{5}[- \frac{u^{3}}{3} + 25 u]_{-5}^{5} \\ &=\frac{1}{5}(((125)+(- \frac{125}{3}))-((-125)+(\frac{125}{3}))) \\ &=\frac{1}{5}(\frac{500}{3}) \\ &=\frac{100}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required area, we will use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$  

Note that the changes of variables

$$
u=8 x - 2 y,\,v=x + y
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required area, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Substituting $8 x - 2 y=u$ and $x + y=v$ into the equation of the first curve, we get

$$
(8 x - 2 y)^{2}-(x + y)=0\,⟹\,u^{2}-v=0\,⟹\,v=u^{2}.
$$

while substituting $x + y=v$ into the equation of the second curve, we obtain

$$
v=16.
$$

To find the intersections of the curves in the $uv$-plane, we solve the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\{\begin{aligned}v=u^{2} \\ v=16\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,u=\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection points are $(\pm 4,16).$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane has the type I representation

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,-4\le u\le 4,\,u^{2}\le v\le 16\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x}&\frac{∂u}{∂y}\\\frac{∂v}{∂x}&\frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{matrix}\right| \\ &=\left|\begin{matrix}8&-2\\1&1\end{matrix}\right| \\ &=10\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=(10)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$  In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Compute the required area.

We calculate the required area by performing the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_D dxdy &=\iint_Δ |\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,dudv \\ &=\iint_Δ |\frac{1}{10}|\,dudv \\ &=\frac{1}{10}\int_{-4}^{4}[\int_{u^{2}}^{16}dv]du \\ &=\frac{1}{10}\int_{-4}^{4}[v]_{u^{2}}^{16}du \\ &=\frac{1}{10}\int_{-4}^{4}(16)-(u^{2})du \\ &=\frac{1}{10}\int_{-4}^{4}(16 - u^{2})du \\ &=\frac{1}{10}[- \frac{u^{3}}{3} + 16 u]_{-4}^{4} \\ &=\frac{1}{10}(((64)+(- \frac{64}{3}))-((-64)+(\frac{64}{3}))) \\ &=\frac{1}{10}(\frac{256}{3}) \\ &=\frac{128}{15}\end{aligned}
$$
